title: L&T and Tata to Exit Ayodhya Ram Mandir by June 30
excerpt: After four years of construction, India's two biggest corporate builders hand the temple back to its trust — for good.
body:
Larsen & Toubro and Tata Consulting Engineers are days away from closing the books on one of modern India's most consequential construction projects. Construction Committee Chairman Nripendra Mishra confirmed that both firms will exit the Ram Mandir site in Ayodhya by June 30, marking the formal end of their involvement in a ₹1,900-crore national undertaking.

**What is happening:**
Mishra told ANI on April 30 that 99 per cent of construction work stands complete, with the *Dhwajdand* — the temple's sacred flagpole — now installed atop the *shikhar* (main spire). A *Pran Pratishtha* ceremony for the Ram Darbar, housing idols of Lord Ram, Mata Sita, and Hanuman ji on the first floor, is scheduled for June 5. One or two days after that ceremony, the full complex opens to pilgrims.

**Why this handover matters:**
Both L&T and Tata Consulting Engineers volunteered their services for the project, signing agreements with the trust in November 2020. Upon exit, each firm extends a three-year warranty on all work performed. The Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust will absorb all outstanding agreements with L&T, Tata, and the Uttar Pradesh State Construction Corporation. Of the total ₹1,900-crore budget, roughly ₹1,600 crore — including GST — has already been disbursed. A small maintenance team from both companies will remain on site.

**What to watch:**
All eyes now turn to the June 5 consecration ceremony — to which no political leaders have been invited — and whether the Teerth Kshetra Trust smoothly assumes stewardship of the 67-acre complex as pilgrim footfall, already between 75,000 and one lakh daily, continues to climb.
